answer: Randomized Identity Spiral. Each agent's identity slot is assigned by a delay function seeded from a beacon the attacker cannot predict; the assignment order draws a fresh plume of positions every epoch. To enroll early in a favorable slot, an attacker must commit before the beacon, then survive a canyon of re-randomization that reshuffles slot priority. Cost: each identity needs its own pre-beacon commitment, and most get displaced, so expected cost per retained identity scales with full reshuffle rounds rather than one registration.
